conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes 'True' for the U.S. FDA-approved use, stating that Kyleena is FDA-approved to prevent pregnancy for up to five years with high cumulative efficacy over that period. Therefore, it clearly endorses the claim.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: True (for U.S. FDA-approved use).** Kyleena, a 19.5-mg levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, is FDA-approved/indicated to prevent pregnancy **for up to five years**. The FDA-approved label says it must be removed by the end of year five; if ongoing contraception is wanted, it may be replaced then. This means five years is the labeled maximum duration—not evidence that the same device remains approved or reliably effective beyond that point. [FDA label](https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/nda/2016/208224Orig1s000LBL.pdf)

**Evidence behind the duration:** The prescribing information explicitly states the indication: prevention of pregnancy for up to five years. The U.S. National Library of Medicine’s DailyMed reproduces the official drug-label information. [DailyMed label](https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080)

The supporting contraceptive-efficacy study enrolled 1,452 generally healthy parous and nulliparous women aged 18–35. Reported results included a first-year Pearl Index of 0.16 (two pregnancies per the study reporting) and an estimated cumulative five-year pregnancy rate of 1.45% (13 pregnancies; upper 95% confidence limit 2.53%), corresponding to about 98.6% cumulative efficacy over five years. [Official HCP efficacy summary](https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy)

These data support the claim for the studied population, while individual suitability and risks require clinician assessment.
